text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms-1 . The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is : (g = 10 m s -2 ) [2022]
explanation: The power delivered by the motor to the lift can be calculated using the formula: Power = Force x Velocity In this case, the force is the sum of the weight of the lift and the passengers and the frictional force opposing the motion: Force = (Weight of lift + passengers) + Frictional force Weight of lift + passengers = Mass x gravity = (2000 kg / 1000) x 10 m/s2 = 20,000 N Therefore, Force = (20,000 N) + (3000 N) = 23,000 N Now, using the formula for power, we get: Power = Force x Velocity = (23,000 N) x (1.5 m/s) = 34,500 W Therefore, the minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is 34,500 W.
